questions.question: What is p→q logically equivalent to?
Which form is equivalent to original implication?
What is the necessary condition in p→q?
What is the sufficient condition in p→q?
Are converse and inverse logically equivalent?
questions.explanation: Converse and inverse are contrapositives of each other.

questions.question: What phenomenon occurs when an implication has a false antecedent?
questions.explanation: An implication with a false hypothesis is vacuously true regardless of the consequent.

questions.question: What type of conditional is based purely on truth values?
questions.explanation: Material implication is the standard truth-functional conditional in classical logic.

questions.question: What is the only false case for p→q?
What does 'p unless q' translate to?
questions.explanation: Unless introduces a negated antecedent; ¬q→p ≡ p∨q.

questions.question: What is the negation of p→q?
questions.explanation: A negated implication keeps the antecedent true and denies the consequent.

questions.question: What is the converse of the contrapositive ¬q→¬p?
questions.explanation: Swapping the contrapositive yields the inverse of the original.

questions.question: 'p is necessary for q' translates to which formula?
questions.explanation: The necessary condition is the consequent.
